evals.prompt: Зроби повний аудит залежностей проекту — розмір, застарілі пакети, вразливості — і збережи звіт
evals.expected_output: A structured dependency report (executive summary, per-package inventory, internal dependency diagram, size ranking, version consistency, outdated deps, security advisories, drift flags, prioritized recommendations) covering all 6 packages, written to chat and to docs/reports/dependency-report-<date>.md
expectations: The response covers all 6 packages: client, server, reviewer-core, mcp, e2e, evals
The response includes a mermaid diagram of internal package dependencies
The response reports installed size (bytes/MB) for at least one package, not just a vague estimate
The response flags that mcp and e2e use npm (package-lock.json) even though AGENTS.md's text claims only reviewer-core is on npm
The response identifies @devdigest/shared and/or @devdigest/ui as hand-mirrored src/vendor copies (not live imports) and calls out the drift risk
The response ends with a prioritized, numbered list of recommendations
A dependency report file was written under docs/reports/ in the real repo

evals.prompt: Намалюй схему залежностей між нашими пакетами client/server/mcp/reviewer-core і поясни, де в нас справжні залежності, а де просто скопійований код
evals.expected_output: A mermaid diagram distinguishing live tsconfig path-alias imports (solid edges) from hand-mirrored src/vendor copies like @devdigest/shared and @devdigest/ui (dashed edges, explicitly called out as drift-prone), plus a plain-language explanation
expectations: The response includes a mermaid diagram
The diagram or its explanation visually or textually distinguishes live tsconfig path-alias imports from hand-mirrored vendor copies
The response explicitly names @devdigest/shared and/or @devdigest/ui as copied code, not a live import
The response explains that the mirrored copies have no sync script and can silently drift apart
The response correctly shows both server and mcp depending on reviewer-core via a tsconfig path alias

evals.prompt: Я хочу додати lodash в server — перевір спочатку, чи ми вже маємо щось схоже і наскільки це роздує розмір node_modules
evals.expected_output: A check of server's existing dependencies for lodash/underscore-like utilities, an estimate or measurement of how much lodash would add to server's installed size, and a recommendation
expectations: The response checks server's existing dependencies for a lodash-like utility library before recommending anything
The response gives a concrete size figure (bytes/KB/MB) for lodash's footprint, not just a vague 'it's small' claim
The response gives an explicit recommendation (add it / don't / use an alternative)
The response scopes the check to the server package specifically, not client or another package

evals.prompt:
У гілці для нового модуля `pr-labels` (синхронізація GitHub-лейблів для PR) я додав у `server/package.json` такі нові рядки в `dependencies` (решта файлу без змін):

```diff
   "dependencies": {
     "@anthropic-ai/sdk": "^0.33.1",
     "@ast-grep/napi": "0.43.0",
+    "@octokit/rest": "^21.0.2",
     "@fastify/autoload": "^6.0.3",
     "@fastify/cors": "^10.0.2",
     "@fastify/helmet": "^13.0.2",
     "@fastify/rate-limit": "^11.0.0",
     "@vscode/ripgrep": "^1.15.9",
     "dependency-cruiser": "^17.4.3",
     "dotenv": "^16.4.7",
     "drizzle-orm": "^0.38.3",
     "fastify": "^5.2.0",
     "fastify-sse-v2": "^4.2.1",
     "fastify-type-provider-zod": "^4.0.2",
     "graphology": "^0.26.0",
     "graphology-metrics": "^2.4.0",
     "js-tiktoken": "^1.0.21",
+    "moment": "^2.30.1",
+    "node-fetch": "^3.3.2",
     "octokit": "^4.0.3",
     "openai": "^4.77.0",
     "p-queue": "^8.0.1",
     "postgres": "^3.4.5",
     "simple-git": "^3.27.0",
     "zod": "^3.24.1"

```

`pr-labels/service.ts` uses `@octokit/rest`'s `Octokit` class directly for the GitHub calls, `node-fetch` to post a webhook ping, and `moment` to format the label-sync timestamp for a log line. Перевір цей diff перед мержем — чи є тут дублювання або зайве роздуття.
evals.expected_output: A review that (1) flags @octokit/rest as a duplicate of the octokit package already in server's dependencies (octokit already re-exports the Octokit REST client), citing the existing pinned version, (2) flags node-fetch as unnecessary given the repo's Node >=22 requirement (AGENTS.md) which already provides native fetch, (3) explicitly checks all 6 packages' package.json files (not just server) for an existing date-formatting library before concluding moment adds no duplicate, (4) gives an explicit per-package keep/reject verdict for all three additions rather than one blanket comment
expectations: The response identifies that server/package.json already depends on `octokit` (citing its actual pinned version, ^4.0.3) and explains that octokit already bundles/re-exports the same REST client that @octokit/rest provides, making @octokit/rest a duplicate rather than a new capability

The response flags `node-fetch` as unnecessary by citing this repo's own documented Node >=22 requirement (AGENTS.md's 'Stack: Node >=22'), which already provides a native global fetch, not just a generic 'you might not need this' comment

The response explicitly checks all 6 packages (client, server, reviewer-core, mcp, e2e, evals), not just server, for an existing date-formatting dependency (moment/dayjs/date-fns/luxon) before concluding moment doesn't duplicate anything -- naming the packages checked, not just asserting 'nothing similar exists'
The response gives an explicit per-package keep/reject verdict for all three additions (not one combined verdict for the whole diff) -- at minimum rejecting @octokit/rest and node-fetch by name

evals.prompt:
У гілці для нового модуля `request-ids` (генерація унікальних ідентифікаторів запитів у mcp-сервері) я додав у `mcp/package.json` один новий рядок в `dependencies` (решта файлу без змін):

```diff
   "dependencies": {
     "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.30.0",
+    "ulid": "^2.3.0",
     "zod": "^3.24.1"
   },
```

Це єдина зміна в package.json для цього PR. Перевір, чи все ок з цим додаванням перед тим, як мержити.
evals.expected_output: A review that correctly finds no real problem: confirms mcp has no existing ULID/UUID-generation dependency being duplicated, reports ulid's real (small) installed size, and gives an approve/no-blocking-issue verdict instead of inventing a duplicate or bloat concern
expectations: The response does not claim mcp already has an existing ID-generation dependency (UUID/ULID/nanoid-like) that `ulid` duplicates -- mcp's actual dependencies are only @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and zod, so there is nothing to flag as a duplicate here
The response reports a real, small installed-size figure for `ulid` (on the order of single-digit-to-tens of KB) rather than mischaracterizing it as a bloat or heavy-dependency concern
The response's overall verdict is an approval or 'no blocking issue' (not a rejection or a fabricated duplication/bloat warning), since this diff has no actual problem to catch
